clue.text: Not up to frolic, wait around

definitions.meaning: to frolic is to kick up one's heels; without the word up the idiom is what remains
to idle away time waiting impatiently

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful definition: the idiom for frolicking, kick up one's heels, with 'up' removed ('Not up') leaves the four-four-five phrase meaning to wait idly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone idly passing time while waiting, so waiting around is its plain meaning.

clue.text: Wet blanket appearing to amuse girl greatly

definitions.meaning: a spoilsport who dampens other people's fun
to kill someone is to amuse them hugely (you kill me), and the girl is Joy, so this reads as killing Joy

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: 'kill' in the sense of make someone laugh a lot, applied to a girl called Joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport who ruins everyone's enjoyment is described by the same compound word as a wet blanket.

clue.text: Frank's given a note to examinee

parts.note: frank means candid, open and honest
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Frank, a student, is handed a note before an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is a person sitting an examination, so an examinee.

clue.text: Love getting role in moving picture, apparently

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An actor in love lands a part in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving picture' suggests a film, but the answer is the optical art movement whose paintings appear to move; 'apparently' signals that illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art uses optical illusions so its static images seem to shimmer and move, apparently a moving picture.

clue.text: Service still on air

parts.note: still and even both mean yet more, as in still better or even better
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A church service is still being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On air' reads as broadcasting, but 'on' is only a link and 'air' is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening church service of the Anglican church.

clue.text: Gangster employed in mob as messenger

indicators.note: the gangster is put to work inside the crowd, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a herd is a mob or crowd
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, so AL

explanation.surface: A mobster working within a gang acts as its go-between.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald was an official who carried and proclaimed messages, so a messenger.

clue.text: Embrace some women compassionately

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man hugs some women in a caring way.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to surround or include, the figurative sense of embrace as in embracing many ideas.

clue.text: Son — man's offspring

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
a pawn is a chess man

explanation.surface: A son is simply a man's child.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the pieces are called men, so 'man' gives PAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn means the offspring or brood produced by a creature, often used of children.

clue.text: Trouble-maker to play a part in hit

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little trouble-maker
to act is to play a part on stage

explanation.surface: A naughty child is cast in a hit show.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is a collision or blow, the noun hit as in a direct hit.

clue.text: Descent with rope taking a considerable time

parts.note: a line is a rope, as on a ship
an age is a long time, as in waiting for ages

explanation.surface: A climber's descent by rope takes a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' suggests abseiling, but it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, the line of descent from one's forebears.

clue.text: Convert working miracle

indicators.note: working means being reworked, so the letters of miracle are put to new use in a new order

explanation.surface: A preacher's conversion of a sinner is a miracle at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim someone is to reform or convert them from wrongdoing; land can also be reclaimed for use.

clue.text: Shared a cigarette with grass

definitions.meaning: held in common, as a combined account
grass is slang for cannabis, so a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: Two friends passed a cannabis cigarette between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint as an adjective means held in common by two or more, and as a noun is slang for a cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: When — returning to Quixote's home, Henry leaves Spanish city

indicators.note: returning means the word for when is read backwards

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: Henry departs, so his letter is removed from the region's name

parts.note: Don Quixote came from La Mancha in central Spain
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Coming back to Don Quixote's homeland, a man named Henry sets off for a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns AS into SA; 'leaves' takes H out of LAMANCHA to give LAMANCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamanca is a historic university city in western Spain.

clue.text: Unknown being paid in yen

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities
earning is being paid for work

explanation.surface: Someone mysterious is paid in Japanese currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like the Japanese money but is the word for a longing; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a strong longing or craving, a synonym of yearning.

clue.text: Displaying no bias, teachers may welcome Head of Eton to meeting

indicators.note: the teachers' union takes in a guest, so one letter goes inside the union's initials

parts.note: NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Teachers fairly welcome the Eton headmaster to their conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may welcome' puts E (from 'Head of Eton') inside NUT to give NEUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting neutrally means taking no side, so showing no bias.

clue.text: Rodent made sheep and cat both turn tail

indicators.note: turning tail means each animal's word is read back to front where it stands

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A rodent made a sheep and a cat both flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both turn tail' reverses each piece in place: RAM becomes MAR and TOM becomes MOT; 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmot is a large burrowing rodent of the squirrel family.

clue.text: Emperor exacting stomach-turning revenge

definitions.meaning: the Aztec ruler conquered by the Spanish
travellers' diarrhoea in Mexico is jokingly called this ruler's revenge

explanation.surface: An emperor wreaks a revenge that turns stomachs.
explanation.definitionFit: Montezuma was the Aztec emperor, and his name is attached to a bout of traveller's diarrhoea.

clue.text: Faith two develop — does it matter?

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters of the two words are reworked

explanation.surface: Faith grows between two people, but who cares?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a dismissive retort asking why something should matter.

clue.text: Vet carefully dictated method of payment

indicators.note: dictated means spoken out for someone to write down, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: to check something is to vet it carefully

explanation.surface: An accountant carefully vets a payment method someone dictates.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money, a method of payment.

clue.text: Plate seen in church, Catholic church

parts.note: Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: Collection plate spotted in a Catholic church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' suggests the collection plate; it means to coat with metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium plating, and to chrome a metal object is to plate it.

clue.text: Horse in old story

definitions.meaning: a stale joke or tale told too often

explanation.surface: A horse appears in an old tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a horse of reddish-brown colour and also a hoary old joke or story.

clue.text: Plate ruined by rain and wet

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Dinner plates are spoilt by being left out in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinware is tinplate, goods made of tin-coated sheet metal.

clue.text: Times featured in memoranda sent over to church worker

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so the multiplication sign goes inside
sent over means turned over, so the word for memoranda is read backwards

parts.note: notes are memoranda
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A Times article appears in memos sent to a church employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent over' turns NOTES into SETON; X goes inside it. 'Times' looks like the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton looks after a church and churchyard, ringing bells and digging graves.

clue.text: Revive first of runners with unusual rest-cure

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word that follows
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of rest-cure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Runners are revived with an unusual rest-cure.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurrect is to bring back to life, so to revive.

clue.text: Variety of brush

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters of brush appear in another form

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the anagram of BRUSH, and brush in the sense of scrubby vegetation, of which this woody plant is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Brush means undergrowth, and a woody bush is one kind of that vegetation.

clue.text: Rear, enforcing discipline

definitions.meaning: the back end of a ship

explanation.surface: A strict parent is backing an unruly child.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern is the back part of a ship and also means strict or severe.

clue.text: Worsted by sudden escalation in sound

indicators.note: in sound means when heard spoken, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rise or escalation

explanation.surface: Someone is beaten by a sudden rise in noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worsted' reads as defeated; it is the woollen fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled worsted fabric.

clue.text: Sales outlet rented out — it was swift

parts.note: a mart is a market, a place where goods are sold
let means rented out, as a flat

explanation.surface: A shop was quickly let to tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swift' looks like an adjective, but it is the bird; martlet was an old name for the swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Martlet is an old word for the swift or martin, the bird now shown footless in heraldry.

clue.text: Intended to do revision of compound equation

parts.note: for means intended to do, as in a knife for cutting

indicators.note: revision means reworking, so the letters of the compound's name are rearranged

parts.note: alum is a chemical compound, a double sulphate of aluminium

explanation.surface: A student plans to revise a chemical compound's equation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision of' rearranges ALUM, the compound, into MULA, an anagram of a synonym rather than of clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a mathematical or chemical statement such as an equation.

clue.text: Not understood by untanned people? It's intolerable

definitions.meaning: beyond meaning out of reach of understanding, and the pale read as pale-skinned people
unacceptable, outside the limits of decent behaviour

explanation.surface: Fair-skinned folk can't grasp something that is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The pale was originally a fenced boundary, such as the English Pale round Dublin; the question mark flags the punning first half, and 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means outside the limits of acceptable behaviour, hence intolerable.
